stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches to study dark matter and dark energy
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has been successfully launched after funding challenges.
It is en route to the L2 Lagrange point for an unprecedented cosmic survey.
The telescope is designed to study fundamental cosmological questions like dark matter and dark energy.

stories.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Major music publishers (Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell) are suing Anthropic.
The lawsuit alleges unauthorized use of tens of thousands of copyrighted musical works by Anthropic.
The financial stakes are high, with potential damages up to $150,000 per work.

stories.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
stories.author: Ola Shorinwa
bullet_points: Introduces CLAP, a new framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation.
Addresses a limitation in current models by allowing training on diverse, internet-scale videos from human and robotic agents.
Aims to enable zero-shot physical simulation by leveraging heterogeneous video data to learn generalizable physics.

stories.title: Token-Level Advertising
stories.author: Qi Qi
bullet_points: Proposes Latent Advertiser Mixture Auction (LAMA), a novel token-level advertising mechanism.
Addresses the challenge of traditional advertising in the context of generative AI's dynamic content creation.
Integrates advertiser influence directly into the AI generation process via local continuation values.

stories.title: Arbitrary code execution in QubesOS via copy-to-VM error reporting backchannel
stories.author: vntok
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability (Arbitrary Code Execution) was found in QubesOS.
The exploit leverages an error reporting backchannel mechanism related to copy-to-VM operations.
This represents a significant security flaw in a major security-focused operating system.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is categorized under key AI/ML tags like 'transformers' and 'llama'.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary application.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance to the large language model ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model designed specifically for autonomous agents.
The model excels at multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured $88 million in funding.
The funding round involved prominent investors including Benchmark, Y Combinator, and 8VC.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when running with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updates result in faster response times and reduced memory consumption.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
A key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
The framework includes built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Federal judge ruled that Trump's blacklisting of Anthropic based on its stance against 'woke' issues was illegal.
Anthropic has publicly opposed the development of lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance technologies.
The ruling highlights legal challenges related to political interference in AI development and corporate policy.

stories.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
stories.author: Haoliang Li
bullet_points: Introduces RedEvoAgent, an automatic red-teaming agent designed to evolve its skills based on experience.
Highlights the increased risk posed by LLM agents in production environments due to potential harmful tool use and state changes, beyond simple text generation.
Addresses limitations in current red-teaming methods, specifically the risk of retrieval bias in trajectory-based attack coordination.

stories.title: CorporateBench: Large-Scale Q&A Benchmarking with Temporal Knowledge Bases
stories.author: Igor Labutov
bullet_points: Introduces CorporateBench (CB), a large-scale, human-validated Q&A benchmark designed for enterprise-scale document collections.
Addresses the critical evaluation gap in LLMs by providing a realistic testing environment that avoids the privacy issues of internal corporate data.
Evaluates LLMs across multiple tasks using a massive corpus exceeding 230,000 documents, focusing on complex, real-world corporate communication scenarios.

stories.title: Omarchy: Any User Process Can Escalate to Root
stories.author: 0xcc.io via ucirello
bullet_points: The news details a critical security vulnerability named 'Omarchy'.
The vulnerability allows any user process to escalate privileges to root access.
This represents a severe security flaw with high potential impact on system integrity.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-source LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It augments Ollama's existing MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: Texas Governor Abbott blocks funding for more Flock cameras
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Texas Governor Abbott has halted state funding for Flock AI surveillance cameras amid public backlash.
A Texas Tribune investigation revealed the state has spent over $30 million on the Flock camera system.
The funding for these cameras was largely sourced through a $1 fee added to insurance policies.

stories.title: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
stories.author: Paresh Dave, WIRED.com
bullet_points: Meta is actively piloting the use of robotics within its data centers.
The robots are being tested on tasks currently performed by human technicians.
This signals a trend toward automation in large-scale infrastructure maintenance.

stories.title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
stories.author: Reece Rodgers, wired.com
bullet_points: Privacy requests sent to 100 companies often resulted in confusion or lack of resolution.
The study highlights significant friction points in how companies handle user data deletion requests.
This points to systemic issues in data governance and user privacy compliance across industries.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized agent experience into persistent, reusable knowledge.
It addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities through interaction by systematizing skill reuse.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM software engineering agents: relying solely on successful trajectories for fine-tuning can introduce noisy supervision.
The paper introduces 'SWE-Prime' to improve LLMs' ability to resolve real-world software issues by refining supervision quality.
SWE-Prime aims to move beyond simply using successful trajectories, recognizing that even successful runs can contain ineffective or risky steps.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Current LLM-based code review systems often treat the process as a single, static decision, which is an oversimplification.
Real-world code review is inherently iterative and interactive, involving multi-round dialogue between developers and reviewers.
The paper introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark LLMs against the complex, dynamic nature of realistic code review scenarios.

stories.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
stories.author: Philippe Schwaller
bullet_points: Introduces MAELLE, a new method for predicting chemical reactions using discrete flow matching.
The approach models reactions not as molecular topology edits, but as transformations in electron occupation vectors.
This represents a shift from traditional generative or heuristic graph-editing ML models in computational chemistry.

stories.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES) as an architectural pattern for LLM agents.
Addresses the conflict between allowing LLM personas to evolve freely and maintaining traceable, auditable execution.
Separates persona (which can drift) and execution (which must be faceless and audited) into distinct trust domains.

stories.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
stories.author: Indranil Sanyal
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in current AI model security scanner evaluation, which often only measure successful judgments.
Researchers benchmark three existing scanners (ModelScan, ModelAudit, Fickling) using a controlled, artifact-backed synthetic corpus.
The evaluation covers 170 Pickle and PyTorch artifacts across 145 specimen families, testing both known and intentional vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: The study addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices in modern critical care.
Researchers developed a novel AI model to learn a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories.
The model was validated using a retrospective, two-site cohort study involving over 36,000 adult patients.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) internally structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs can distinguish between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
Researchers use six independent linear probes, one for each MFT category (e.g., care/harm, fairness), to map these relationships geometrically within the models.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in current sepsis severity scoring, which uses outdated, fixed indices.
Proposes a novel machine learning approach to learn a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories.
The study is a retrospective, two-site validation across a large patient cohort (over 36,000 patients).

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge beyond simple content detection.
The study employs six independent linear probes, corresponding to the six categories of Moral Foundations Theory (MFT).
The goal is to determine if LLMs geometrically distinguish between different moral foundations and the relationships between them.

stories.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
stories.author: Wenguang Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost barrier in large language model (LLM) pretraining for academic and open-source communities.
Presents 'Puro-2B,' a cost-efficient method for training a Qwen2-1.5B model using an RTX 5090 within the card's budget.
Contributes to the ongoing effort to democratize LLM development by offering an accessible, open-source training recipe.

stories.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
stories.author: Zhenkun Wang
bullet_points: The paper investigates Evolution Strategies (ES) as a memory-efficient post-training method for Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning.
It systematically compares ES against mainstream methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
The research empirically and theoretically demonstrates that ES offers a performance advantage over GRPO in LLM reasoning.

stories.title: Beyond Parallel Blindness: Information Floors and Model Gaps in Block Drafting
stories.author: Yufei Ding
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in block drafting models, which propose multiple tokens simultaneously.
It introduces an 'information floor' to differentiate between missing path information and imperfect modeling of observable data.
The 'model gap' is defined as rejection exceeding this information floor, offering a new metric for model evaluation across different domains.

stories.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
stories.author: Ting Zhu
bullet_points: Introduces CritICL, a novel inference-time framework designed to improve LLM reasoning.
Addresses the inefficiency of current methods (like repeated generation) used to boost LLM performance.
Leverages the insight that LLM failure modes follow structured patterns across different model scales within the same family.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experiences into reusable skills.
The system addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories.
It enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities by systematically reusing persistent knowledge.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM software debugging by criticizing the reliance on large-scale agent trajectory datasets.
The core problem identified is that successful trajectories used for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) can still contain noisy, redundant, or risky steps.
The proposed method, SWE-Prime, aims to improve LLM performance by refining the supervision signal rather than just increasing dataset size.

stories.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper introduces TTPO (Test-Time Policy Optimization) to address limitations in post-training methods like RL and OPSD for LLMs.
Existing methods rely on ground-truth labels, which prevents effective test-time training (TTT).
TTPO proposes using majority-vote pseudo-labels instead of ground truth, while analyzing the fragility and asymmetry of this approach.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current LLM-based code review systems, which treat the process as a static, single-round task.
It introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark code review against its complex, multi-round, and interactive nature found in real-world software development.
The research aims to move beyond simplified automated checks to model the iterative problem-solving inherent in human code reviews.

stories.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
stories.author: Dongyan Zhao
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) where LLMs suffer from entropy collapse, leading to narrow reasoning coverage.
The proposed solution introduces cross-model non-parametric perturbation as a method to preserve the generative diversity of LLMs during RLVR.
The work aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities while mitigating the degradation in performance (pass@$k$) caused by entropy reduction.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) internally structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs can distinguish between different Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models to map the geometric relationships between these moral foundations.

stories.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
stories.author: Guanhua Chen
bullet_points: Clinical language models often fail in real-world deployment due to overfitting to note-specific artifacts (e.g., templates, boilerplate).
The proposed CAST framework uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAE) to identify and suppress these non-patient-state artifacts.
CAST enables auditable clinical text classification by exposing sparse, human-interpretable features from Transformer activations.

stories.title: WebMCP: Give Browser Agents Tools Instead of Buttons
stories.author: toannhu
bullet_points: Introduces WebMCP, a concept aimed at enhancing browser agents.
Addresses limitations of current AI agents that rely on simple actions like clicking buttons.
Suggests giving agents 'tools' rather than just predefined UI interactions for more complex tasks.
